Phoebe our sister, which is a servant of the church. (v.1)

The Revised Standard Version calls Phoebe a "deaconess", which would make her a church leader. If the RSV translation is correct, this verse contradicts the requirement that women not be permitted to teach and that they must be silent in church. (1 Cor.14:34-35, 1 Tim.2:11-12).

Junia ... of note among the apostles (v.7)

Was there a woman apostle? That is how some interpret this verse and use it to justify a more active role for women in the church.

Can women be church leaders?

Some translators were so upset at the idea of a woman apostle that they replaced "Junia" with "Junias." The problem with this is that although "Junia" was a common woman's name at that time, there is no evidence for "Junias" as a man's name.
